question.text: Let $z_{1}, z_{2}$ be two fixed complex numbers in the argand plane and $z$ be an arbitrary point satisfying $\left|z-z_{1}\right|+\left|z-z_{2}\right|=2\left|z_{1}-z_{2}\right|$. Then, the locus of $z$ will be

options.text: a bisector of the line segment joining $z_1$ and $z_2$

solution.text:
We know that $\left|z-z_{1}\right|+\left|z-z_{2}\right|=k$ will represent an ellipse, if $\left|z_{1}-z_{2}\right|    < k$
Hence. the equation $\left|z-z_{1}\right|+\left|z-z_{2}\right|$ $=2\left|z_{1}-z_{2}\right|$ represent an ellipse.
